$comment: The only place a hostname is written. `base_domain` was bought at LiveDNS and the staging CNAMEs were created 2026-08-26; the staging hosts below are the custom subdomains (swapped 2026-08-27) and app/core/cors.py builds the credentialed-request allowlist from them. The frontends additionally need the api host BAKED IN at build time as VITE_API_ORIGIN (a Railway service variable on each static service -- see web/packages/core/src/identity/session.ts), so a host change here means setting that variable to match and redeploying the three apps. PRODUCTION (2026-08-30) is on Railway's GENERATED domains, not custom subdomains of base_domain, and that is a deliberate staging point rather than the end state: a custom host needs a CNAME at LiveDNS, and until DNS resolves the environment would be unreachable -- a working production on an ugly hostname beats a pretty one that 404s. Swapping to api/staff/app/admin.gladiatorclub.co.il later is: add the domain in Railway, change the four hosts here, redeploy the api so CORS re-reads this file, then set VITE_API_ORIGIN on the three frontends and rebuild them so the new origin is baked in.
$transitional_comment: TEMPORARY, and it has a removal condition. Production's custom domains come alive one at a time as Let's Encrypt issues each certificate, so for a while the three apps are split across two hostnames: `staff` reachable ONLY at gladiatorclub.co.il, `parent` and `dashboard` ONLY at their Railway hosts. Switching `environments.production` wholesale would refuse the two that still work; leaving it alone refuses the one that does -- which is what happened, and it renders a sign-in screen with no sign-in buttons, because the app cannot fetch /auth/providers. So both sets are allowed until every certificate has issued. DELETE this key and `transitional_origins` at that point, and move the four hosts in `environments.production` to the custom domains in the same commit -- app_origin() reads those and decides where OAuth returns a signed-in user, so it must not name a host that cannot serve.
